question: How can SCSS architecture affect CSS performance?
shortAnswer: Bloated compiled CSS increases download/parse; unused includes and duplicate mixin output add weight.
detailedAnswer: Prefer shared classes, purge unused, and avoid generating exhaustive utility matrices without need.

question: Does nesting depth hurt runtime performance?
shortAnswer: Selector matching is usually not the bottleneck today; payload size and unused CSS matter more.
detailedAnswer: Still avoid pathological selectors. Measure rather than mythologize selector speed.

question: How do you prevent unused SCSS from shipping?
shortAnswer: Modular @use (don't load unused components), PurgeCSS/content scans, and route-level CSS splitting.
detailedAnswer: Global main importing everything is a common SPA footgun.

question: Scenario: compiled CSS is 2MB from Sass maps generating every color utility.
shortAnswer: Generate fewer utilities, use CSS variables + open-ended classes, or on-demand generation.
detailedAnswer: Data-driven generation needs budgets. Not every token needs a class.

question: @extend performance/maintainability concerns?
shortAnswer: Can merge selectors in ways that create large groups and unexpected coupling across files.
detailedAnswer: Often mixins or real shared classes are clearer. Profile output if using extend heavily.

question: Sass compile time too slow in CI — fixes?
shortAnswer: Reduce @import duplication (use @use once), simplify giant loops, upgrade Dart Sass, and cache builds.
detailedAnswer: Generation of thousands of classes dominates. Split entrypoints.

question: Critical rendering path: how SCSS delivery strategy helps?
shortAnswer: Split critical vs deferred CSS, inline critical carefully, and defer non-route styles.
detailedAnswer: Architecture that isolates route CSS enables this. Monolithic CSS blocks rendering.

question: Are complex :nth-child selectors from SCSS loops costly?
shortAnswer: Can be harder to maintain and occasionally costly in complex DOMs; prefer classes for stateful styling.
detailedAnswer: Generate clear class hooks instead of relying on structural selectors for core UI.

question: CSS containment / content-visibility vs SCSS role?
shortAnswer: SCSS can't replace modern rendering optimizations — emit rules that enable containment where useful.
detailedAnswer: Understand browser features; preprocessor is orthogonal but should not fight them.

question: Duplicated media queries from nested @media — problem?
shortAnswer: Slightly larger CSS; gzip mitigates repeated selectors/media text often — still keep breakpoints tidy.
detailedAnswer: PostCSS tools can sort/merge sometimes. Prefer clarity first; optimize with metrics.

question: How do source maps relate to SCSS performance debugging?
shortAnswer: They map minified CSS back to partials for DevTools — essential for finding bloat sources.
detailedAnswer: Ensure production can disable maps publicly while keeping internal access.

question: Lead: set a CSS performance budget for Sass-heavy apps.
shortAnswer: Max KB per route, unused CSS %, compile time SLO, and CI fail on regressions.
detailedAnswer: Own budgets with design system team. Pair with LCP/INP monitoring.

question: When do icon fonts in SCSS pipelines hurt performance?
shortAnswer: Large font payloads, FOIT/FOUT, and extra glyphs; prefer SVG sprites/inline SVGs.
detailedAnswer: Don't @include entire icon font for three icons. Tree-limit glyph sets.

question: Best practice: token CSS variables vs generating many color classes?
shortAnswer: Variables + a few utilities often smaller and more flexible than combinatorial class explosions.
detailedAnswer: Generate only what product uses. Measure gzipped CSS.
